title: Review and resume tenant settings changes
summary: Export tenant settings to YAML, plan field-level differences, and apply reviewed updates sequentially. Resume throttled export, plan, or apply operations with --continue rather than replaying completed requests.
scope: Tenant-scoped admin REST operations; do not pass --workspace. Capacity, domain, and workspace delegated overrides are not part of this workflow.

format.desired: schemaVersion: 1, kind: tenant-settings, tenantId, endpoint, settings. Each setting has settingName, metadata, and values.
format.supported_values: enabled, enabledSecurityGroups, excludedSecurityGroups. Group entries use graphId and optional name; order and display-name-only differences do not cause updates.
format.limitations: Delegation flags and advanced properties are preserved as read-only metadata in this workflow, not editable values. This is an implementation limit, not a statement that the underlying API cannot update them.
format.checkpoint_names: Defaults append .export.checkpoint.yaml or .plan.checkpoint.yaml to --out, or .apply.checkpoint.yaml to the apply input plan. Completed checkpoints are retained.
format.failure_metadata: error.progress contains counts and the checkpoint path; error.retry_after and error.retry_at are included when a valid Retry-After was supplied.

workflow: Export with admin export-tenant-settings --out tenant-settings.yaml and keep a private original backup.
Edit supported desired values without changing the schema version, tenant binding, or metadata; omitted settings remain unmanaged.
Use admin plan-tenant-settings --file tenant-settings.yaml --out tenant-plan.yaml and review the before/after changes.
Preview with admin apply-tenant-settings --file tenant-plan.yaml --dry-run; ask the user to approve tenant-wide changes before applying.
Apply the reviewed plan with admin apply-tenant-settings --file tenant-plan.yaml --continuation-file apply-state.yaml.
If interrupted, follow the error hint and resume the same operation with --continue <checkpoint-file>.
quota_and_recovery: The workflow accommodates the conservative 25-requests/hour budget in the feature request. The service's actual Retry-After response is authoritative; do not assume a fixed quota window or that the caller has the full budget available.
Throttling stops the workflow and persists progress instead of entering the ordinary short automatic retry loop. RATE_LIMITED uses exit code 7; wait as instructed before continuing.
--continue is a checkpoint-file option, not the global --continuation-token pagination option. Do not combine it with fresh-run file/output arguments.
Completed snapshot pages and acknowledged setting updates are not replayed. Uncertain write outcomes need reconciliation before another write.
Keep input files unchanged, retain checkpoint files, use the same authenticated tenant, and never edit checkpoint contents.
Preserve private files and consistent paths between CI jobs. Do not run concurrent resumes of the same checkpoint or blindly restart the original apply command.
safety: Tenant setting changes can affect every workspace. Preview and obtain approval; apply respects --readonly.
Changed live baselines require replanning, not --force. Offline dry-run cannot verify live state.
Apply is sequential, not transactional. Partial success is possible; there is no automatic rollback.
A restoration requires its own reviewed plan using the captured original values. Do not overwrite another administrator's changes.
Checkpoints do not store authentication credentials, but contain sensitive tenant configuration and group identifiers; keep them access-controlled.
output: Export and plan write YAML files. Stdout uses normal Fabio output helpers and summarizes artifacts and execution.
Presentation flags do not truncate or transform saved configuration or planned work.
A no-change plan contains no updates; missing settings never mean delete or disable.
Inspect destructive markers and warnings before running apply without --dry-run.
